sred.technicalChallenge: Whether the existing Avaturn avatar and Mixamo-derived clips can be retargeted into a physics-driven locomotion state machine, and whether a hero-to-game transition can share one rendering canvas and avatar skeleton without the talking scene and the game scene competing for control, within the 60 FPS desktop / 30 FPS mobile and 8 MB additional-asset budgets.
sred.approachAndResult: Retargeted the existing Avaturn avatar to Mixamo-derived clips with a baked clothing fix and drove it with a Rapier fixed-step kinematic controller, sharing one React Three Fiber canvas between the talking hero and the game through a session state machine. Iterated over 12 QA rounds and 3 Codex cross-review rounds: slope and step handling, grounded landing, a sphere-cast follow camera with line-of-sight and body-clearance solving (round 1 of the final review found the camera could be pushed past the solved clear distance; fixed by bounding it and clipping the avatar with the near plane), worker-based procedural texture painting and batched shader warm-up. Result: 60 FPS (vsync-bound, render CPU p95 0.8 ms) on an M1 Pro at 1440x900 and 1920x1080 and under 4x CPU-throttled phone emulation, about 0.95 MB extra first-play download against an 8 MB budget, cold Play-to-swap cut from about 1.3 s to 0.7 s, no resource growth over 50 entry and exit cycles, and every failure row recovering to a usable portfolio; mobile performance on a physical device remains unmeasured.
